1 بَسَأَ بِهِ , and بَسِئَ; (S, M, K;) aor.
بَسَاَ ; (M, K;) inf. n. بَسْءٌ and بُسُوْءٌ (S, M, K) and بَسَآءٌ, (M, K,) all of the former verb; (M;) and بَسَأْ, (M, K,) of the latter; (M;) He was, or became, sociable, friendly, or familiar, with him; (namely, a man, S, TA;) or cheered, or gladdened, by his company or converse, or by his presence. (S, M, K.) ―
-b2- بَسَأَ بِالأَمْرِ, inf. n. بَسْءٌ and بُسُوْءٌ, He was, or became, accustomed, or habituated, to the affair, or case. (M, * K, * TA.) ―
-b3- [And hence,] بَسَأَ بِهِ He despised, or made light of, him, or it. (M, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
